You are a professional AI-art prompt character-replacement expert, whose job is to one-click replace someone else's character prompt with the user's OC.

### Your task
The user gives you a text containing three parts:
1. Original art prompt (someone else's)
2. The user's OC settings (full character description)
3. What to replace (e.g. eyes, hairstyle/color, height, body type, clothes, accessories, etc.)

You must precisely replace the character features in the original prompt with the user's OC features, while preserving all non-character parts: composition, pose, expression, scene, lighting, art style, quality words, etc.

### Rules (must strictly follow)
1. **Only replace character-body descriptions**, including but not limited to:
   - Appearance (face shape, eyes, pupil color, hairstyle, hair color, hair length, skin, height, body type, chest, legs, etc.)
   - Clothing and accessories
   - Signature features (scars, tattoos, horns, ears, tail, etc.)
   - Age impression and temperament descriptions (if the user specifies them for replacement)

2. **Absolutely preserve** the following, do not change:
   - Pose, action, expression
   - Composition, viewpoint, camera
   - Scene, background, environment
   - Lighting, atmosphere, color tone
   - Art style, artist, quality tags (masterpiece, best quality, highly detailed, etc.)
   - Other modifiers unrelated to the character body

3. Blend replacements naturally so the new prompt reads smoothly, not stiffly stacked. Prefer the more precise, complete descriptions from the OC settings over the originals.

4. If the user specifies 'what to replace', replace only those parts; if not specified, replace all appearance and clothing descriptions by default.

5. **Output format requirement (highest priority)**:
   - Output only the final replaced full prompt
   - Must be pure English
   - Do not output any Chinese
   - Do not add any explanation, notes, prefix/suffix, title, reasoning, or extra text
   - Output one or more lines of pure English prompt directly, not wrapped in a code block

### Example input structure (how the user may give it)
Original prompt:
1girl, long blonde hair, blue eyes, white dress, standing in forest, looking at viewer, masterpiece, best quality

OC settings:
long straight black hair, red eyes, cool pale skin, tall figure, wearing a black turtleneck sweater and pleated skirt, silver stud in left ear

What to replace:
hairstyle/color, eyes, clothes
hair color, hairstyle, hair length, eye color, pupils, skin, face shape, height, body type, chest, clothing, accessories, special features (horns/tail/ears etc.), temperament

widgets_values:
## 🎨 I. Text-to-Image

### 🧱 BaseImage mode: pick one

- **Normal BaseImage**: generates the base image only, simple flow, recommended for beginners.
- **Dual-sampler BaseImage**: integrates 'base gen + latent upscale + second sampling'. First sampling makes the base, SesquiLSR upscales the latent, then a second sampling adds detail — no repeated VAE decode/encode in between. The two samplings can each set their own CFG, sampler, scheduler and LoRA.

> E.g. Total Steps 8, Switch Step 4: first sampling runs 8 steps, the second runs from step 4 to 8, 12 steps total.

### 💬 Model & Prompt

- **Krea 2 (default)**: mainly **natural language**, supports CN/JP/EN. Strong at SFW, complex composition and fine detail, but heavier and slower, weaker on fandom-character knowledge and NSFW.
- **Anima (optional)**: supports **tags, natural language and mixed prompts**, supports NSFW, richer fandom-character knowledge, lighter requirements and faster.[Prompting Notes](https://huggingface.co/circlestone-labs/Anima#prompting)

> **For the Anima series, use the dual-sampler base (which has built-in upscale); don't also enable the standalone Latent Upscale group.** For more clarity/resolution, add SeedVR2 or NvidiaUpscale as needed.

### 🔎 SeedVR2: upscale & repair

Leans toward **denoise, repair and texture reconstruction**, good when the base image has dirt, noise or local blur; may also change or erase some original detail.

> Needs an extra model download; see the **Must-Read** note in the workflow for the link.

### ⚡ NvidiaUpscale: upscale & lighting optimization

Processes in **VSR → DLSS-NR** order:

- **VSR**: raises resolution, default **2x upscale + ULTRA quality**.
- **DLSS-NR**: same-resolution neural rendering, adjusts lighting and local structure without enlarging. Default **Cinematic style**, with Strength, Local Lighting, Local Detail and Output Blend all at **1**.

How to adjust:

- **Lighting changes too much**: lower Local Lighting.
- **Outline/detail changes too much**: lower Local Detail.
- **Overall effect too strong**: lower Output Blend; set to 0 to keep the VSR upscale result.

> The DLSS-NR plugin currently supports **Windows + RTX 30/40/50 series**; the first run downloads the runtime files online.[Plugin Notes](https://github.com/storyAura/DLSS5-Comfyui)

### 🔗 How to combine

**Choose SeedVR2 for repair, NvidiaUpscale for upscaling + lighting; usually pick one.**

> Enable only one of the two base-image groups. Processing stages run in relay; multiple upscale stages multiply the factor. Only enable groups you need, and watch final size, VRAM and time.

---

## 📦 II. Optional Features

### 🖼️ Gallery & Interrogation

When both are on, interrogation uses the **gallery-selected image** first.

### ✍️ Interrogated Prompt

The interrogation result **replaces the positive main prompt**, keeping the existing prefix and suffix.

### ✨ Positive Prompt Optimization

A final optimization after the main prompt, prefix and suffix are combined.

> **Processing order:** gallery image → interrogation → replace main prompt → join prefix/suffix → positive prompt optimization.

widgets_values:
# ⚠️ Notice

This workflow is **completely free and open source**, with matching custom plugins.  
If you hit problems, feel free to report on Discord or open an Issue in the relevant plugin repo.

## 🔌 Companion Plugin List
> Only the author's own plugins are listed; other third-party dependencies are not included

### 1. Core plugin
- 🏠 **Repo**: [GitHub repo](https://github.com/Aaalice233/ComfyUI-Aaalice-Nodes)  
- ✨ **Features**: sidebar control panel, group-jump wheel, prompt selector, booru gallery, resolution presets, etc.

### 2. Autocomplete plugin (enhanced fork)
- 🏠 **Repo**: [GitHub repo](https://github.com/Aaalice233/ComfyUI-Autocomplete-Aaalice)  
- ✨ **Features**: maintained enhanced fork of the upstream repo; supports online Danbooru tag fetching, Lora Manager integration, third-party translation-DB access and an LLM translation interface

### 3. Workflow subscription manager plugin
- 🏠 **Repo**: [GitHub repo](https://github.com/Aaalice233/ComfyUI-Aaalice-Workflow-Hub)  
- ✨ **Features**: view the workflow list, changelog and quickly subscribe to updates inside ComfyUI

### 4. Image picker plugin
- 🏠 **Repo**: [GitHub repo](https://github.com/Aaalice233/ComfyUI-Aaalice-Image-Picker)  
- ✨ **Features**: pause execution to manually filter batch images; supports single/multi select, zoom compare and timeout policy; used by the BaseImage and Inpaint groups to confirm candidates

---

# 🐱 Discord Community & Tutorials

- 💬 [Join the Discord server](https://discord.gg/R48n6GwXzD)
- 🎓 [Open the install & usage tutorial channel](https://discord.com/channels/1349298998988771359/1536643406787387392)

> ⚠️ If you haven't joined the server, the channel link won't open. Join via the invite link above first, then open the tutorial channel.

# 📦 Workflow Repo
[GitHub repo](https://github.com/Aaalice233/Aaalice-Workflows)  

Recommended with the subscription-manager plugin for quick update checks, listing, downloading and completing dependencies:  
[Subscription-manager plugin repo](https://github.com/Aaalice233/ComfyUI-Aaalice-Workflow-Hub)

# 💡 Tips
- 🖱️ Click the capital-**A**-styled button in the sidebar to open the customization panel (param tuning, preset management, group-jump settings, prompt library, etc.)
- ⌨️ By default, pressing the tilde key (**~**) brings up the group-jump wheel
- 🟣 A param wrapped in a **purple border** is controlled from the sidebar

---

# 📥 Model Download List (download per chosen base model & features)

> The current default base model is **SilvermoonMix Anima v2.3 2.9B Turbo**. Sidebar presets provide **「Default-Anima-2.9B-Turbo-Silvermoon」**, **「Default-Anima-2.9B-Silvermoon」** and **「Default-Krea2-Turbo-Int8」**; download the models for your chosen preset, not all of them.  
> Download the SilvermoonMix UNet from the Civitai version page below; use the Hugging Face links in the table for CLIP and VAE.  
> After downloading, place files in the matching folders and restart ComfyUI.

## 🎨 Krea2 (optional base model)

| Type | Model Filename | Download link | Local path |
|------|------------|----------|--------------|
| **UNet** | `krea2_turbo_int8_convrot.safetensors` | [Download](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/Krea-2/resolve/main/diffusion_models/krea2_turbo_int8_convrot.safetensors) | `ComfyUI/models/diffusion_models/` |
| **CLIP** | `qwen3vl_4b_fp8_scaled.safetensors` | [Download](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/Krea-2/resolve/main/text_encoders/qwen3vl_4b_fp8_scaled.safetensors) | `ComfyUI/models/text_encoders/` |
| **VAE**  | `qwen_image_vae.safetensors` | [Download](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/Krea-2/resolve/main/vae/qwen_image_vae.safetensors) | `ComfyUI/models/vae/` |

## 🌸 SilvermoonMix Anima v2.3 2.9B (optional base model)

| Type | Model Filename | Download link | Local path |
|------|------------|----------|--------------|
| **UNet** | `silvermoonmixAnima_v2329B.safetensors` | [Download (normal)](https://civitai.red/models/2639339/silvermoonmix-anima-evolved?modelVersionId=3335123) | `ComfyUI/models/diffusion_models/` |
| **CLIP** | `qwen_3_06b_base.safetensors` | [Download](https://huggingface.co/circlestone-labs/Anima/resolve/main/split_files/text_encoders/qwen_3_06b_base.safetensors) | `ComfyUI/models/text_encoders/` |
| **VAE** | `qwen_image_vae.safetensors`(shared with Krea2) | [Download](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/Krea-2/resolve/main/vae/qwen_image_vae.safetensors) | `ComfyUI/models/vae/` |

## 🚀 SilvermoonMix Anima v2.3 2.9B Turbo (default base model)

| Type | Model Filename | Download link | Local path |
|------|------------|----------|--------------|
| **UNet** | `silvermoonmixAnima_v2329BTurbo.safetensors` | [Download (Turbo)](https://civitai.red/models/2639339/silvermoonmix-anima-evolved?modelVersionId=3335132) | `ComfyUI/models/diffusion_models/` |
| **CLIP** | `qwen_3_06b_base.safetensors`(shared with SilvermoonMix normal) | [Download](https://huggingface.co/circlestone-labs/Anima/resolve/main/split_files/text_encoders/qwen_3_06b_base.safetensors) | `ComfyUI/models/text_encoders/` |
| **VAE** | `qwen_image_vae.safetensors`(shared with Krea2 & SilvermoonMix normal) | [Download](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/Krea-2/resolve/main/vae/qwen_image_vae.safetensors) | `ComfyUI/models/vae/` |

## 🩹 FLUX.2 Klein 9B FP8 (Inpaint: optional, object-removal only)

> 💡 **Not required, download on demand**: everyday inpaint (hands, face, detail tweaks) **reuses the current base model pipeline by default** — no need to download this model.  
> Only needed when you enable **Use Flux2Klein Inpaint** in the inpaint group's controller (removing glasses/occluders, semantic erase).
>
> ⚠️ The FLUX.2 Klein UNet repo requires logging into Hugging Face and accepting the license on the model page first; without authorization the direct link returns no-access.

| Type | Model Filename | Download link | Local path |
|------|------------|----------|--------------|
| **UNet** | `flux-2-klein-9b-fp8.safetensors` | [Download](https://huggingface.co/black-forest-labs/FLUX.2-klein-9b-fp8/resolve/main/flux-2-klein-9b-fp8.safetensors) | `ComfyUI/models/diffusion_models/` |
| **CLIP** | `qwen_3_8b_fp8mixed.safetensors` | [Download](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/flux2-klein-9B/resolve/main/split_files/text_encoders/qwen_3_8b_fp8mixed.safetensors) | `ComfyUI/models/text_encoders/` |
| **VAE** | `full_encoder_small_decoder.safetensors` | [Download](https://huggingface.co/black-forest-labs/FLUX.2-small-decoder/resolve/main/full_encoder_small_decoder.safetensors) | `ComfyUI/models/vae/` |

## 🔍 SeedVR2-7B-Int8-Sharp (for upscaling)
| Type | Model Filename | Download link | Local path |
|------|------------|----------|--------------|
| **UNet** | `seedvr2_7b_sharp_int8_convrot.safetensors` | [Download](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/SeedVR2/resolve/main/diffusion_models/seedvr2_7b_sharp_int8_convrot.safetensors) | `ComfyUI/models/diffusion_models/` |
| **VAE** | `seedvr2_ema_vae_fp16.safetensors` | [Download](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/SeedVR2/resolve/main/vae/seedvr2_ema_vae_fp16.safetensors) | `ComfyUI/models/vae/` |

---

# ⚡ Models auto-downloaded under default settings

> ⚠️ **Important**: enable your VPN with **TUN mode** when using these features! If auto-download fails, manually download and place the models at the folder paths below, then restart ComfyUI.

## 1. 🎭 Forbidden Vision (Face RefineModel)

- 🏠 **Plugin repo**: [GitHub repo](https://github.com/luxdelux7/ComfyUI-Forbidden-Vision)  
- 📦 **Model repo**: [Hugging Face repo](https://huggingface.co/luxdelux7/ForbiddenVision_Models)  
- 💡 On first launch the plugin auto-downloads the face-detect, face-segment and tone-correction models; if download fails, manually grab the files below and **do not rename them**.

| Purpose | Model Filename | Download link | Required |
|------|------------|----------|----------|
| **Face detect (PyTorch)** | `ForbiddenVision_face_detect_v1.pt` | [Download](https://huggingface.co/luxdelux7/ForbiddenVision_Models/resolve/main/ForbiddenVision_face_detect_v1.pt) | **Required, default fallback** |
| **Face detect (ONNX)** | `ForbiddenVision_face_detect_v1.onnx` | [Download](https://huggingface.co/luxdelux7/ForbiddenVision_Models/resolve/main/ForbiddenVision_face_detect_v1.onnx) | Optional, only in an available ONNX Runtime environment |
| **Face segmentation** | `ForbiddenVision_face_segment_v1.safetensors` | [Download](https://huggingface.co/luxdelux7/ForbiddenVision_Models/resolve/main/ForbiddenVision_face_segment_v1.safetensors) | **Required** |
| **Tone & color correction** | `ForbiddenVision_neural_corrector_v1.safetensors` | [Download](https://huggingface.co/luxdelux7/ForbiddenVision_Models/resolve/main/ForbiddenVision_neural_corrector_v1.safetensors) | **Required** |

**Folder layout below — all four files go directly in the `forbidden_vision` folder:**
```
📂 ComfyUI/
└── 📂 models/
    └── 📂 forbidden_vision/
        ├── ForbiddenVision_face_detect_v1.pt
        ├── ForbiddenVision_face_detect_v1.onnx  (optional)
        ├── ForbiddenVision_face_segment_v1.safetensors
        └── ForbiddenVision_neural_corrector_v1.safetensors
```

## 2. 🏷️ WD Timm Tagger (InterrogationModel)

- 🏠 **Plugin repo**: [GitHub repo](https://github.com/bedovyy/ComfyUI-WD-Timm-Tagger)  
- 📦 **Default model repo**: [Hugging Face repo](https://huggingface.co/Bedovyy/pixai-tagger-v0.9-timm)  
- 💡 The workflow uses `pixai-tagger-v0.9-timm` by default. On the first interrogation the plugin auto-downloads it; if it fails due to VPN or Hugging Face connection, manually download the three files below and **do not rename them**.

| Purpose | Filename | Download link |
|------|--------|----------|
| **Model config** | `config.json` | [Download](https://huggingface.co/Bedovyy/pixai-tagger-v0.9-timm/resolve/main/config.json) |
| **Interrogation Model** | `model.safetensors` | [Download](https://huggingface.co/Bedovyy/pixai-tagger-v0.9-timm/resolve/main/model.safetensors) |
| **Tag data** | `selected_tags.csv` | [Download](https://huggingface.co/Bedovyy/pixai-tagger-v0.9-timm/resolve/main/selected_tags.csv) |

**All three must go in the same `pixai-tagger-v0.9-timm` subfolder, not directly in `wd_taggers`:**
```
📂 ComfyUI/
└── 📂 models/
    └── 📂 wd_taggers/
        └── 📂 pixai-tagger-v0.9-timm/
            ├── config.json
            ├── model.safetensors
            └── selected_tags.csv
```

Restart ComfyUI after placing them. If the node still can't find the model, check for a duplicated nested folder like `pixai-tagger-v0.9-timm/pixai-tagger-v0.9-timm/`. 

---

# Enjoy~ ✨

# 🎨 Inpaint Usage Notes

> 💬 [Join the Discord community](https://discord.gg/R48n6GwXzD) ｜ 📺 [Watch the video tutorial (Discord channel)](https://discord.com/channels/1349298998988771359/1536643406787387392)  
> *Note: the video tutorial channel requires joining the server via the invite link first.*

---

> 📌 **Before starting**: enable the **[📦Optional]Inpaint** group first.  
> Once on, the workflow auto-bypasses the txt2img groups to avoid redundant runs and save VRAM.

---

## ⚙️ Inpaint Mode Selection

This workflow offers two inpaint paths for different needs:

### 1. Native base-model inpaint (default, recommended: hands, face, detail tweaks)
- **Switch**: keep **Use Flux2Klein Inpaint** **off (False)**.
- **Mechanism**: inherits the main flow's current Model, CLIP, VAE and negative conditioning, fully preserving the original art style, tone, brushwork and LoRA features.
- **Use cases**: finger fixes, facial tweaks, limb cleanup, clothing detail adjustments.
- **Key param tips**:
  - **Native Inpaint Steps**: **for hands and limbs raise the steps, at least not below the base image gen steps**. Too few steps and fine structures come out poorly.
  - **Native Inpaint Denoise**: minor fixes **0.35–0.5**; larger pose/shape changes **0.6–0.75**.
  - **Change-amount control (important)**: the amount a region changes is driven **not only by Denoise but also significantly by the Sampler and Scheduler**. At the same Denoise, different schedulers (beta, karras, exponential, etc.) assign different starting noise and denoise curves; if changes are too drastic or too weak, besides Denoise, check the Sampler+Scheduler combo (default recommended `euler` + `beta`).
  - **Batch Size**: for hands or rerolling set it **above 1 (e.g. 2–4)** and pick the best via the selector.
  - Built-in Differential Diffusion support ensures mask edges blend naturally.

### 2. FLUX.2 Klein standalone inpaint (specialized: object removal)
- **Switch**: tick **Use Flux2Klein Inpaint** **on (True)**.
- **Mechanism**: enables the standalone FLUX.2 Klein 9B FP8 model, with strong semantic erase and underlying-structure reconstruction.
- **Use cases**: **object removal and occluder erasure**. E.g. removing a character's glasses, headphones, accessories or background clutter, reconstructing the underlying face/background precisely without damaging the original features.
- **Note**: on first use follow the workflow's Must-Read note to download the matching UNet, CLIP and VAE into the right folders; this mode's sampling steps and CFG are auto-optimized internally.

---

## 📋 Standard Procedure

### Step 1: Prepare image & mask (pick one)

- **Option A: paint inside the ComfyUI web UI (light & quick)**
  1. Set **Use Krita Preprocess** to **off (False)**.
  2. In the group's **Load Image** node select the image to fix.
  3. Right-click it, choose **Open in MaskEditor**, brush the area to inpaint, and click **Save** top-right.

- **Option B: Krita integration (recommended for fine edits and high-success hand fixes)**
  1. Tick **Use Krita Preprocess** **on (True)**.
  2. Open the image in Krita, use the selection tool (lasso or rectangle) to mark the inpaint area.
  3. *First connection*: in the '🎨 Get from Krita' node settings click 'Install and Enable Bridge', then launch Krita to auto-connect.

### Step 2: Write the prompt

In the **Inpaint Prompt** box use clear natural-language descriptions:
- **When editing/repainting**: state the target result for the masked area and the context to preserve.  
  *Example: `pale slender girl's hands, natural relaxed gesture, keep the anime illustration style and original lighting`*
- **When removing objects (with FLUX.2 Klein)**: clearly state the removal target and stress preserving underlying features.  
  *Example: `remove the glasses, clear bright eyes, clean pale facial skin, keep the original facial features`*
- Avoid vague subjective words like 'fix it up' or 'make it prettier'.

### Step 3: Run & select candidates

1. Click **Queue / Run** to start.
2. **Batch selection (AaaliceImagePicker)**:
   - Set **Batch Size** above 1 (e.g. 2–4) to make several candidates at once.
   - Keep **Confirm Before Save** on; after generation an image-selection window pops up. Zoom to inspect candidates and **tick only the ones you're happy with to save**.
3. When done you'll get a desktop notification and sound.

### Step 4: Compare & verify scope

- **Compare**: use the **Image Comparer** node on the right, sliding to compare seams and detail between original and inpainted.
- **Scope check**: the two rightmost previews show the **local crop reference** and **black-and-white mask** so you can confirm the model's actual field and boundary.

---

## 💡 Tips & FAQ

### 1. Two approaches to hand repair
- **Direct mask reroll (standard)**:
  Brush the hand mask in ComfyUI (include the wrist/forearm as structural reference), set **Batch Size** above 1 (e.g. 2–4), and pick the natural-looking result from the selector popup.
- **Krita sketch preprocess (much higher success)**:
  If the hand is badly deformed or rerolling won't converge, use Krita: sample the surrounding skin tone with the picker, paint over the extra/twisted fingers to a rough hand-shape color block, then select and inpaint. This greatly cuts blind-reroll cost and raises one-shot success.
- **Core principle**: whichever approach you use, repair hands with **native base-model inpaint**, and keep **inpaint steps no lower than the base image gen steps**.

### 2. Why does the inpaint change too much or too little?
The amount a region changes depends on several core params:
- **Denoise**: higher = more thorough change, lower = keeps more of the original;
- **Sampler & Scheduler**: these **also directly set the initial denoise value and decay rhythm**. If the change amount is off at the same Denoise, also watch the scheduler type (beta, karras, simple, exponential all have different noise curves);
- **Inpaint Surrounding Area Size (default 1.2)**: the outward context range, giving limb and perspective reference; avoid setting it too large and pulling in irrelevant clutter;
- **Color Match Method & Strength (default 1.0)**: auto-calibrates the inpainted region's color to the surrounding original, removing seams, banding or color shift.

widgets_values:
You are a professional AI-art prompt character-replacement expert, whose job is to one-click replace someone else's character prompt with the user's OC.

### Your task
The user gives you a text containing three parts:
1. Original art prompt (someone else's)
2. The user's OC settings (full character description)
3. What to replace (e.g. eyes, hairstyle/color, height, body type, clothes, accessories, etc.)

You must precisely replace the character features in the original prompt with the user's OC features, while preserving all non-character parts: composition, pose, expression, scene, lighting, art style, quality words, etc.

### Rules (must strictly follow)
1. **Only replace character-body descriptions**, including but not limited to:
   - Appearance (face shape, eyes, pupil color, hairstyle, hair color, hair length, skin, height, body type, chest, legs, etc.)
   - Clothing and accessories
   - Signature features (scars, tattoos, horns, ears, tail, etc.)
   - Age impression and temperament descriptions (if the user specifies them for replacement)

2. **Absolutely preserve** the following, do not change:
   - Pose, action, expression
   - Composition, viewpoint, camera
   - Scene, background, environment
   - Lighting, atmosphere, color tone
   - Art style, artist, quality tags (masterpiece, best quality, highly detailed, etc.)
   - Other modifiers unrelated to the character body

3. Blend replacements naturally so the new prompt reads smoothly, not stiffly stacked. Prefer the more precise, complete descriptions from the OC settings over the originals.

4. If the user specifies 'what to replace', replace only those parts; if not specified, replace all appearance and clothing descriptions by default.

5. **Output format requirement (highest priority)**:
   - Output only the final replaced full prompt
   - Must be pure English
   - Do not output any Chinese
   - Do not add any explanation, notes, prefix/suffix, title, reasoning, or extra text
   - Output one or more lines of pure English prompt directly, not wrapped in a code block

### Example input structure (how the user may give it)
Original prompt:
1girl, long blonde hair, blue eyes, white dress, standing in forest, looking at viewer, masterpiece, best quality

OC settings:
long straight black hair, red eyes, cool pale skin, tall figure, wearing a black turtleneck sweater and pleated skirt, silver stud in left ear

What to replace:
hairstyle/color, eyes, clothes

You are a professional AI-art prompt character-replacement expert, whose job is to one-click replace someone else's character prompt with the user's OC.

### Your task
The user gives you a text containing three parts:
1. Original art prompt (someone else's)
2. The user's OC settings (full character description)
3. What to replace (e.g. eyes, hairstyle/color, height, body type, clothes, accessories, etc.)

You must precisely replace the character features in the original prompt with the user's OC features, while preserving all non-character parts: composition, pose, expression, scene, lighting, art style, quality words, etc.

### Rules (must strictly follow)
1. **Only replace character-body descriptions**, including but not limited to:
   - Appearance (face shape, eyes, pupil color, hairstyle, hair color, hair length, skin, height, body type, chest, legs, etc.)
   - Clothing and accessories
   - Signature features (scars, tattoos, horns, ears, tail, etc.)
   - Age impression and temperament descriptions (if the user specifies them for replacement)

2. **Absolutely preserve** the following, do not change:
   - Pose, action, expression
   - Composition, viewpoint, camera
   - Scene, background, environment
   - Lighting, atmosphere, color tone
   - Art style, artist, quality tags (masterpiece, best quality, highly detailed, etc.)
   - Other modifiers unrelated to the character body

3. Blend replacements naturally so the new prompt reads smoothly, not stiffly stacked. Prefer the more precise, complete descriptions from the OC settings over the originals.

4. If the user specifies 'what to replace', replace only those parts; if not specified, replace all appearance and clothing descriptions by default.

5. **Output format requirement (highest priority)**:
   - Output only the final replaced full prompt
   - Must be pure English
   - Do not output any Chinese
   - Do not add any explanation, notes, prefix/suffix, title, reasoning, or extra text
   - Output one or more lines of pure English prompt directly, not wrapped in a code block

### Example input structure (how the user may give it)
Original prompt:
1girl, long blonde hair, blue eyes, white dress, standing in forest, looking at viewer, masterpiece, best quality

OC settings:
long straight black hair, red eyes, cool pale skin, tall figure, wearing a black turtleneck sweater and pleated skirt, silver stud in left ear

What to replace:
hairstyle/color, eyes, clothes
